subject: Math
prompt:
$$g(t)=5000(1.003)^{4}t$$

The given function $g$ models the value of an investment account, in dollars, $t$ years after it is opened. Which statement is the best interpretation of $(1.003)^{4}t$?

choices.A: At the end of every $3$-month interval, the value increases by about $0.3%$ of the value at the beginning of the $3$-month interval.
choices.B: Every $4$ months, the value increases by about $$3$.
choices.C: Every $3$ months, the value increases by about $$3$.
choices.D: At the end of every $4$-month interval, the value increases by about $0.3%$ of the value at the beginning of the $4$-month interval.

explanation: Choice A is correct. In an exponential growth function of the form $a(1+r)^{nt}$, the base $(1+r)$ represents $1$ plus the growth rate per compounding period, and the exponent coefficient $n$ represents the number of compounding periods per unit time. For the expression $(1.003)^{4t}$, the base is $1.003 = 1 + 0.003 = 1 + 0.3\%$, indicating a $0.3\%$ growth rate per compounding period. The exponent $4t$ means that when $t = 1$ year, there are $4$ compounding periods, so the investment compounds $4$ times per year. Since there are $12$ months in a year, dividing $12$ by $4$ gives $3$ months per compounding period. Therefore, at the end of every $3$-month interval (quarterly), the account value increases by about $0.3\%$ of the value at the beginning of that $3$-month interval.
